proposal.summary: The requester (SH-CX) asked for a chatbot explaining parcel lateness, assuming a communication gap (CL-01). Investigation found 300/1000 orders (30%) late at the handover stage (E-02), with 290 of those released only after carrier pickup already occurred and 21/30 RELEASE-BATCH runs failing (E-04) — a warehouse-side release bottleneck, not a communication issue (H-COMMUNICATION-GAP rejected). The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring critical unknowns about handoff data integrity and batch-failure root cause as verification obligations (VOBs), and the release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: only the pickup-timing correlation work item (W-WI-1, correlate_pickup_timing on DA-PICK) was actually released, while chatbot delivery, batch-failure diagnosis, handover analysis, and the pickup-schedule push remain withheld.
key_points: Root cause as established: 30% handover-stage lateness (E-02) driven primarily by a warehouse RELEASE-BATCH bottleneck — 21/30 run failures and 290 orders released after pickup (E-04/F-03/F-04) — not by carrier pickup delay alone (E-01 median 2.0h, E-06 uniform across slots) nor a pure communication gap.

The initial request (chatbot for communication gap, CL-01 from SH-CX) was tested as hypothesis H-COMMUNICATION-GAP and REJECTED, contradicted by E-04; H-WAREHOUSE-PROCESSING-DELAY and H-WMS-BATCH-FAILURE are SUPPORTED by E-04.

SH-LOG's competing claim (CL-02/E-03, carrier picks up two hours late) is non-authoritative and numerically consistent with E-01 but does not account for the 290-order release-after-pickup finding (E-04).
Only one action was released: correlate_pickup_timing on DA-PICK (work item W-WI-1, status DONE), matching the solution design's minimum_useful_scope and release_scope.

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the DEFINE gate was CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred critical unknowns tracked as open VOBs (VOB-U-HANDOFF-DATA-INTEGRITY, VOB-U-BATCH-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE, VOB-R-3) whose blocking scope lies outside what was released.

push_pickup_schedule is a protected action requiring mandatory carrier human approval (K-SCHED, grounded in carrier contract §3 / E-05) and was withheld because its supporting hypothesis H-SCHEDULE-APPROVAL-BOTTLENECK is only CANDIDATE and unknown U-SCHEDULE-APPROVAL-CONTRIBUTI remains OPEN.

deliver_delay_explanation, diagnose_release_batch_failures and analyze_handover_lateness remain withheld because they depend on resolving VOB-U-HANDOFF-DATA-INTEGRITY and VOB-U-BATCH-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE, both still open.
limitations_explained: Any future pickup schedule change still requires mandatory carrier human approval under K-SCHED (E-05) and cannot be automated end-to-end.

The system cannot yet diagnose why RELEASE-BATCH fails or validate the Shop-to-Carrier handoff, so batch-failure diagnosis, handover-lateness analysis, and customer-facing delay explanations are withheld pending resolution of VOB-U-BATCH-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE and VOB-U-HANDOFF-DATA-INTEGRITY.
Whether approval-step friction under K-SCHED contributes to the 2.0h pickup delay is unresolved (unknown U-SCHEDULE-APPROVAL-CONTRIBUTI is OPEN; VOB-R-3 open), so push_pickup_schedule stays withheld.

Establishing a cross-org handoff validation process (SR-HANDOFF-VALIDATION-PROCESS) to confirm H-PICK's delivery_status/semantic_validity was judged infeasible in contest time, so handoff integrity cannot be closed this cycle.

Underlying assumptions remain unverified: that the 30% handover late rate overlaps with the 290 released-after-pickup orders (A-HANDOVER-RELEASE-OVERLAP), that batch failures directly cause lateness rather than merely correlate (A-RELEASE-FAILURES-CAUSE-DELAY), and that the sampled data (E-01, E-02, E-04) is representative despite unknown completeness of DA-ORD and DA-WMS (A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVENESS).
